explain.say: Pumped storage hydro uses two lakes at different heights. When there is spare electricity, such as at night or on windy days, it is used to run pumps.

faq.q: How does pumped storage store energy?
faq.a: It uses electricity to pump water uphill into a high reservoir, turning electrical energy into gravitational potential energy. Letting the water fall back through turbines turns it back into electricity.

faq.q: How much energy can pumped storage hold?
faq.a: It depends on how much water there is and how far it falls. Dinorwig in Wales can deliver about 1.7 gigawatts for around 5 hours, roughly 9 gigawatt-hours in all.

faq.q: How fast can pumped storage start?
faq.a: Very fast. Dinorwig can go from standby to full power in well under a minute, so it is used to catch sudden jumps in demand, such as everyone switching on kettles at once.
asks: Why is pumped storage good for sudden demand?

faq.a: About 70 to 80 percent of the electricity used to pump the water comes back. The rest is lost to friction in the pipes and to heat in the pumps, turbines and generators.
asks: How much energy is lost in pumped storage?

faq.q: Why don't we build more pumped storage?
faq.a: It needs two big reservoirs close together with a large height difference, which few places have, and it is expensive and slow to build. Big batteries now handle many of the shorter storage jobs.
asks: Where can pumped storage be built?

facts: Measured by the energy it can hold, pumped storage hydro is still the largest form of grid energy storage in the world.
Dinorwig power station in Wales, built in tunnels inside a mountain, can produce about 1.7 gigawatts.
